solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Assortment of big tomes acquired illegally

indicators.note: an assortment is a jumbled mix, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A collection of large books turns out to have been stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: The old past tense of 'beget' with 'mis-' describes something gained or fathered unlawfully, hence obtained by illicit means.

clue.text: Insect in picture given different tail

indicators.note: the word for a picture has its final letter swapped for another one

parts.note: an image is a picture

explanation.surface: An insect appears in a photograph whose end has been altered.
explanation.definitionFit: The adult, fully developed stage of an insect after metamorphosis has this name in entomology.

clue.text: Person holding American playwright to be confusing

indicators.note: one word holds the other, so the playwright sits inside the word for a person

parts.note: a being is a person or creature
Thornton Wilder wrote Our Town

explanation.surface: Someone clutching a US dramatist proves baffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something baffling or perplexing is described with this adjective; both mean hard to understand.

clue.text: Deadly contest good fun somehow? Right not to begin

indicators.note: somehow suggests the three letters are put together in some other way
the word loses its opening letter, being told not to start

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a lethal fight is good fun, and is told that is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges FUN to UNF; 'not to begin' drops the R of RIGHT to leave IGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A shootout with pistols, as in a Western, is a contest that is likely to end in death.

clue.text: Move towards fans quixotically?

parts.note: Don Quixote charged at windmills, whose sails are giant fans, thinking them giants

explanation.surface: Approaching admirers in an idealistic, impractical way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fans' looks like supporters but means the turning sails of windmills, which Cervantes's hero attacked.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to fight imaginary enemies, from the episode in Don Quixote where the knight attacks windmills.

clue.text: Run into trees and laugh uncontrollably

indicators.note: the run goes into the trees, so its letter is placed inside the word

parts.note: a copse is a small group of trees
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A jogger collides with some trees and gets the giggles.
explanation.walkthrough: In theatre slang an actor who breaks into unplanned laughter on stage is said to do this.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre slang: a performer who giggles helplessly during a scene ruins it in this way.

clue.text: Reluctant to talk about US university achieving harmony

indicators.note: the reluctant word goes about, that is around, the university

parts.note: coy means shy or unwilling to reveal things
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A shy student at an American college finds concord.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means courteous, friendly relations, especially between nations, a kind of social accord.

clue.text: Cruel king — he is lacking instrument of punishment

indicators.note: the king's name lacks the letters of the pronoun, which are removed

parts.note: Herod ordered the Massacre of the Innocents
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tyrannical monarch is without his means of chastisement.
explanation.definitionFit: A stick or cane used for beating, as in 'spare the rod', is an implement of corporal punishment.

clue.text: Coastline irregular in parts

indicators.note: an irregular arrangement of the word's letters signals they are reordered

explanation.surface: A jagged shoreline appears in some places.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made of separate pieces or segments, like modular furniture, is divided into sections.

clue.text: New road, not old, going around Lancashire town

indicators.note: turning around means the whole string of letters is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the abbreviation for old is taken out of the word road

explanation.surface: A freshly built bypass skirts a town in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes O from ROAD to give RAD; 'going around' reverses NEWRAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Darwen is a mill town near Blackburn in Lancashire, a county in north-west England.

clue.text: Unsuccessful paper boss in mess backing the French

indicators.note: the mess comes behind, backing up, the French article

parts.note: la is the French feminine for 'the'

indicators.note: the editor goes inside the word for mess

parts.note: muck is dirt or a mess
ED is short for editor, a newspaper's boss

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor in a muddle supports the French, without success.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician serving out a term after losing, or any ineffective person, is called this; used attributively it means ineffectual.

clue.text: Material left at back of court

indicators.note: the letter for left is placed at the back, after the courting word

parts.note: to woo is to court a lover

explanation.surface: Some fabric has been left behind at the rear of a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: Spun sheep's fleece is a textile, so it counts as a fabric or cloth.

clue.text: I sit in cart sprawled out, lacking elegance

indicators.note: the letters are spread about in a new arrangement, as a body sprawls

explanation.surface: Someone lounging in a cart, limbs everywhere, looks ungainly.
explanation.definitionFit: Without artistic taste or skill describes something crude, short on grace and style.

clue.text: Famous institution newly established in this mansion

indicators.note: the letters are set up afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A renowned body has just been founded in a grand house.
explanation.definitionFit: The Washington-based museum and research complex founded with James Smithson's bequest is a renowned institution.

clue.text: Team's facing question about style — not the No.1 attraction

indicators.note: one piece faces the other, standing before it

parts.note: a team is a side, so team's gives side's
'how?' asks about the manner or style of doing something

explanation.surface: A squad confronts questions about its playing manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor show alongside the main event at a fair is a secondary attraction, not the headline.

clue.text: Downtown area you see with deficit, yes!

parts.note: look at the words deficit and yes: the letters c-i-t-y sit inside them, joined across the gap

explanation.surface: An urban district where a shortfall is cheerfully acknowledged.
explanation.walkthrough: The second part describes itself: in 'defiCIT Yes' a four-letter town word lies on the inside, so the answer is a playful description of where it sits.
explanation.definitionFit: The central, often deprived, districts of a large town are its downtown zone in American usage.

clue.text: They are charged and kept in station sometimes

indicators.note: the letters are kept inside the run of two words

explanation.surface: People are detained and charged at the police station now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' suggests arrest, but here it means carrying electric charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Atoms or molecules that have gained or lost electrons carry an electric charge.

clue.text: Beginning to want electronic device, being scared

parts.note: a start is a beginning
an LED is a light-emitting diode

explanation.surface: Someone first wanting a gadget turns out to be frightened.
explanation.definitionFit: Being suddenly alarmed or given a fright is to be made jumpy, a state of sudden fear.

clue.text: Worker, one who votes 'no'?

parts.note: a worker ant is the familiar crossword insect
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A labourer is the one who opposes the motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' does double duty: it gives I and also begins the definition 'one who votes no'.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent of a proposal is called an against-person, from the Latin prefix meaning opposed.

clue.text: Mad, bad place in which the truth resides?

parts.note: nuts means crazy
hell is the worst of places

explanation.surface: A crazy, awful spot is where honesty lives.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'in a nutshell' means stated briefly, so the plain truth can be put there.

clue.text: Good girl over time becomes greedy person

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the rest

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A well-behaved young woman eventually turns into a glutton.
explanation.definitionFit: This seabird is known for gulping fish, so it is British slang for a glutton who eats greedily.

clue.text: Writer of instructions for school getting spelling a bit wrong?

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: one letter of the school's name is misspelt, swapped for another

parts.note: a grammar school is a selective British secondary school

explanation.surface: Someone backing a grammar school can't spell properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting spelling a bit wrong' changes the final A of GRAMMAR to E, the commonest misspelling of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who writes code for computers produces sets of instructions for machines.

clue.text: Operation penetrating bone — word said when knife slips?

indicators.note: the operation pierces the bone, going inside it

parts.note: os is Latin for bone, used in anatomy

explanation.surface: A surgeon cutting into bone exclaims when the scalpel slips.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation of dismay at a small mistake is what one blurts after a slip.

clue.text: Urge to be in corps of journalists

definitions.meaning: to ... someone is to urge them

explanation.surface: Encouraging someone to join the news reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to push or urge, and the noun means newspapers and reporters as a body.

clue.text: Help returning along wiggly line

indicators.note: the word for help comes back, read right to left

parts.note: aid means help

indicators.note: a wiggly version of the word has its letters wriggled around

explanation.surface: Assistance comes back along a wavy path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns AID into DIA; 'wiggly' rearranges ALONG to AGONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A slanting stroke joining opposite corners of a square is a kind of straight line.

clue.text: Dope showing elements of ingenuity

indicators.note: some of the word's elements, a run of its letters, are taken

explanation.surface: An idiot displays signs of cleverness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests a fool, but in slang it also means inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British informal terms for information or facts, as in 'the latest dope'.

clue.text: Garland at front of place of crime in Dutch city

indicators.note: the garland is placed at the front, before the other piece

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian flower garland
a den, as in a den of thieves, is where criminals gather

explanation.surface: A wreath is left at the front of a crime scene in a Netherlands town.
explanation.definitionFit: Leiden is a university city in South Holland, a place in the Netherlands.

clue.text: Young bird starts to chirp — you get nervous, excited, tense

indicators.note: the starts, the opening letters, of the following six words are taken

explanation.surface: A fledgling begins to cheep, and you become jittery and tense.
explanation.definitionFit: The offspring of a swan is called by this name, so it is a juvenile waterfowl.

clue.text: Africans appeal for Europeans to enter

indicators.note: the Europeans enter the word for appeal, going inside it

parts.note: to sue is to appeal or plead, as in suing for peace
Danes are people from Denmark

explanation.surface: People from Africa plead for Europeans to be let in.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Sudan, a country in north-east Africa, are inhabitants of that continent.
